props.title: What the #$*! Do We (K)now!?

sections.content: **What the #$*! Do We Know!?** (2004) sparked intense debate by blending documentary interviews with dramatized sequences starring Marlee Matlin. This unconventional film merged quantum physics concepts with New Age spirituality, launching a wave of consciousness-exploring documentaries. Similar philosophical documentaries like Mindwalk (1990) and I Am (2010) continued probing reality's nature through conversations and visual metaphors.

sections.content: The early 2000s saw several films tackling consciousness and reality through experimental formats. The Matrix (1999) had already primed audiences for questioning reality, while Vanilla Sky (2001) and Mulholland Drive (2001) blurred dreams with waking life. These narratives reflected growing public interest in neuroscience and quantum mechanics' stranger implications. SUBHEAD: Science and Spirituality in Cinema

The film's approach to merging science and spirituality echoes in later works like Another Earth (2011) and Coherence (2013), which use scientific concepts as jumping-off points for exploring human consciousness. Inception (2010) took similar themes mainstream, examining reality layers through blockbuster action rather than documentary format.
